draft.title: The fall of the Qing
card: By the mid-1800s the Qing dynasty was weak. Foreign powers pressed it for trade and land, and it lost wars it could not win.
Revolts at home added to the strain. The Taiping Rebellion, which began in 1850, was a huge revolt that killed many millions of people.
Many Chinese came to blame the Qing for China's weakness. Some Qing rulers were Manchu, from outside the Han majority, and this added to the anger.

In 1911 a revolution broke out and the last emperor gave up the throne in 1912. This ended over 2,000 years of rule by emperors. China became a republic, a state led by a government and not by a monarch.
draft.remember: Pressure from abroad and revolts at home weakened the Qing, and the 1911 revolution replaced the emperor with a republic.

a.q: Which change did the 1911 revolution bring to China?
opts: Rule by emperors ended and a republic was set up
A new emperor took over from a different dynasty
Foreign powers took direct control of the government
The Communist Party took power and ruled the country
a.why: The revolution ended rule by emperors and made China a republic. It did not simply swap one dynasty for another, which is what had happened in earlier changes of rule.
a.clue: Think about what kind of state China became.

b.q: Which statement best explains why the Qing dynasty was weak by 1900?
opts: Foreign pressure and revolts at home wore down its power
Its people had always supported rule by emperors
Its rulers chose to give power to a republic in 1850
One single revolt overthrew it in the early 1800s
b.why: The Qing were worn down over time by foreign pressure and revolts such as the Taiping Rebellion. No single event did it. The 1911 revolution came after this long weakening and was not a sudden break.
b.clue: Look for a cause that built up over many years.

a.best: Rule by emperors ended and a republic was set up

b.best: Foreign pressure and revolts at home wore down its power

problems.detail: "Some Qing rulers were Manchu" is misleading: the Qing was a Manchu dynasty, and all of its emperors were Manchu. It should say the Qing rulers were Manchu.

The why says the 1911 revolution 'was not a sudden break'. This clashes with the card and question a, which present it as ending over 2,000 years of rule by emperors. It also goes beyond what question b asks.

The right option repeats the remember line almost word for word. The distractors are plainly absurd (a republic in 1850, a single revolt in the early 1800s), so the question is too easy for Years 9 and 10.

b.q: A historian argues that the Qing fell in 1911 because of problems that had built up long before. Which fact best supports this?
opts: Decades of revolt had already drained Qing strength
The Qing had beaten foreign powers in earlier wars
Han Chinese had long backed their Manchu rulers
Rule by emperors in China had only just begun
b.why: Revolts such as the Taiping Rebellion, from 1850, strained the Qing for decades, so the dynasty was already weak before 1911. The Qing lost its wars with foreign powers rather than winning them, and anger at the Manchu rulers grew rather than support.
b.clue: Which fact describes a problem that wore the Qing down?
